report.tagline: The UK's biggest supermarket loyalty scheme, giving lower 'Clubcard Prices' and points to members in exchange for their shopping data.
report.simpleSummary: Clubcard is Tesco's free loyalty card. You scan it when you shop and get special lower prices on thousands of items, plus points that turn into vouchers. In return, Tesco learns exactly what you buy. It uses that data to set prices, choose stock and sell targeted ads to brands.

overview.whatItDoes: Clubcard gives members special prices and points. Since 2020, Tesco has shown two prices on shelves: the normal price and a lower 'Clubcard Price'. You only get the lower one if you scan your card. This made Clubcard almost essential for Tesco shoppers.
howItWorks: Sign up free in the Tesco app or in store.
Scan the card at checkout, online or in the app to get Clubcard Prices.
Earn 1 point per £1 spent (2 points per £1 on fuel at Tesco). Every 150 points become a £1.50 voucher.
Spend vouchers at Tesco, or swap them with Reward Partners like restaurants and days out for up to 2x their value.
Tesco and its data business dunnhumby analyse what members buy to set prices and sell targeted ads to brands through Tesco Media and Insight.
overview.valueProposition: Lower prices on everyday shopping and rewards, just for scanning a free card.

businessModel.summary: Clubcard costs Tesco money through discounts and points. In return it brings more shoppers, more frequent visits and detailed data. Tesco earns from that data through better pricing, ads and supplier funding.

revenueStreams.detail: Members shop more often and spend more at Tesco.
Brands pay Tesco Media and Insight to reach Clubcard members.
Brands often fund part of the discount for visibility.
dunnhumby sells insights and tools to suppliers.

businessModel.pricing: Clubcard is free. Clubcard Plus costs £7.99 a month. Points: 1 per £1 in store and online.
costDrivers: Points paid out as vouchers (about 1% of spend)
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a £100 shop, a member might save £5 to £10 through Clubcard Prices and earn £1 in points. Part of the discount is often paid by the brands. Tesco gains because the member shops more often at Tesco, and that data lets Tesco sell targeted ads. Tesco's operating margin is only about 4%, so every point of loyalty matters.

howTheyGetUsers: Clubcard Prices labels in every Tesco store
Partners like Reward Partners and fuel
growth.moat: Clubcard has decades of data on what UK households buy. Tesco uses it to set prices and sell ads. Its size means brands want to work with it. Rivals like Nectar copied the idea, but Tesco's scale is hard to beat.

guardrailMetrics: Customer trust in pricing (complaints and Which? findings)
strengths: Largest loyalty base in UK grocery
Clubcard Prices made the card nearly essential
weaknesses: Non-members pay more, which some see as unfair
Reward Partner value was cut from 3x to 2x in 2023
risks: Regulation on loyalty pricing; Which? raised a complaint to the CMA about unclear Clubcard pricing
Data privacy laws limiting use of data
Discounters winning on simple low prices
userComplaints: Clubcard Prices are not always real savings
Unit prices were not shown on Clubcard deals (Tesco later agreed to show them)
Points expire or vouchers are easy to lose
App issues scanning or loading offers

improvementIdeas.idea: Show 'you saved £X this year' and a price history for Clubcard Price items.
improvementIdeas.problem: Shoppers doubt Clubcard Prices are real deals.

improvementIdeas.idea: Auto-apply vouchers at checkout when the customer chooses.
Simpler Clubcard for older customers with a printed monthly savings summary.
improvementIdeas.problem: Older shoppers struggle with app-only features.

improvementIdeas.idea: Let members choose which data uses they allow, with bonus points for sharing.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More trust and better data consent.

pmLessons: Loyalty schemes are data businesses. Tesco gives small discounts and gets data worth much more.
Member prices can boost sign-ups, but must be fair and clear or they create a trust problem.
Second revenue streams like retail media can pay for customer benefits.
Small changes to rewards, like the Reward Partner cut, can anger loyal users.

interviewQuestions.question: Is Clubcard Prices good or bad for customers?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh savings for members against higher prices for non-members. Discuss fairness and trust. Suggest how to measure.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase Clubcard app use?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find why people use the plastic card. Ideas: digital-only offers, savings tracker. Metric: monthly active app users.

interviewQuestions.question: How does Tesco make money from Clubcard?
interviewQuestions.hint: More visits, retail media, supplier funding, data insights. Compare to cost of discounts and points.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a new Clubcard feature for young shoppers.
interviewQuestions.hint: Understand needs: meal deals, budgets. Ideas: student offers, budget tracker. Metrics: sign-ups and visits.

interviewQuestions.question: What would you do if the CMA banned member-only prices?
interviewQuestions.hint: Plan B: personal offers, points boost, subscriptions. Measure impact on visits and margins.
